passages.title: Client Success: apology for portal outage

text.content:
Dear Mr. Brennan,

I am writing to apologize for the service interruption that affected your online ordering portal on September 9. Our technical team traced the outage to a failed software update.
The portal was restored at 2:40 P.M., and we have [[191]] additional monitoring overnight to prevent a recurrence. [[192]], we have credited your account with one month of hosting fees at no charge.

Please accept our [[193]] for the inconvenience this caused your sales staff. [[194]]

Sincerely,
Priya Nair
Client Success Manager
OrbitWeb Hosting

questions.explanation: The company put new monitoring in place; "implemented" means put into operation.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing a similar-looking verb (implied / imported / impressed) that does not mean put a system into use.

questions.explanation: The fee credit is a second remedy after the monitoring step. "In addition" marks that additive relationship.
questions.commonMistake: Using "On the contrary" when the sentence continues the apology remedies rather than opposing them.

questions.explanation: After "our," a plural noun is required. "Apologies" is the standard phrase for a formal expression of regret.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the verb "apologize" or the adjective "apologetic" where a noun slot after "our" is needed.

passages.title: Product launch: AeroBlend Pro kitchen blender

text.content:
INTRODUCING THE AEROBLEND PRO

KitchenWare Co. is proud to announce the AeroBlend Pro, our most powerful countertop blender yet. Designed for busy cafés and home cooks alike, it delivers restaurant-quality results in under sixty seconds.
The AeroBlend Pro features a [[195]] motor housing that stays cool during long blending cycles. [[196]], every unit ships with a recipe booklet and a two-year limited warranty at no extra cost.

Order before October 31 and [[197]] 15 percent off your first case. [[198]]

Visit kitchenwareco.com/aeroblend or call 1-800-555-0192 to place your wholesale order today.

questions.explanation: Before the noun "motor housing," an adjective is required. "Durable" correctly modifies the housing.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adverb "durably" or the noun "durability" where an adjective slot before a noun is needed.

questions.explanation: The recipe booklet and warranty are extra benefits after the motor feature. "In addition" marks that additive relationship.
questions.commonMistake: Using a contrast connector (Nevertheless / By contrast) when the sentence adds another selling point.

questions.explanation: Customers who order early get a discount; "receive" means obtain that 15 percent off.
questions.commonMistake: Selecting a similar-looking verb (reserve / replace / review) that does not mean obtain a discount.

text.content:
PROTECTING COMPANY DATA AT WORK

Last quarter, Meridian Holdings reported a 40 percent drop in phishing incidents after rolling out a company-wide security awareness campaign. The Information Security Office shares three practices that contributed to that improvement.

First, employees are asked to verify [[199]] requests for password resets by calling the help desk on a known number. [[200]], staff should never click links in unexpected emails that ask for account credentials.

A short online quiz will be [[201]] each month to reinforce these habits. [[202]]

For questions, contact infosec@meridianholdings.com or visit the intranet Security Hub.

questions.explanation: Employees should check password-reset requests that look questionable; "suspicious" means causing distrust.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing a similar-looking adjective (successful / sufficient / subsequent) that does not mean questionable or untrustworthy.

questions.explanation: The second tip adds another security practice. "Moreover" signals that additive relationship between the two guidelines.
questions.commonMistake: Using "Instead" (replacement) or "Consequently" (result) when the sentence simply adds a parallel tip.

questions.explanation: After "will be," a past participle is needed for the passive voice. "Administered" correctly forms "will be administered."
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the base verb "administer" or the noun "administration" where a passive past participle is required.

text.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All third-floor staff
From: Lena Ortiz, Facilities Director
Date: September 14
Subject: Renovation of the east wing conference area

Beginning Monday, September 21, contractors will renovate the east wing conference rooms on the third floor. The project is expected to last approximately three weeks.

During this period, meetings normally held in Rooms 3E and 3F should be [[203]] to the second-floor training center. [[204]], temporary workstations will be set up in the west atrium for employees whose desks are adjacent to the construction zone.

Please pack personal items by Friday so that movers can clear the area [[205]]. [[206]]

Thank you for your cooperation.
Lena Ortiz

questions.explanation: Meetings need to be moved to another space; "relocated" means transferred to a different place.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing a similar-looking verb (recalled / reduced / released) that does not mean move meetings to another room.

questions.explanation: Temporary workstations are an additional accommodation. "Furthermore" adds that second logistical detail.
questions.commonMistake: Using "Nonetheless" (contrast) when the memo continues listing renovation accommodations.

questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify "can clear." "Promptly" means without delay.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adjective "prompt" or the noun "promptness" where an adverb modifying the verb phrase is required.

Thank you for your invoice SF-4481 dated August 28 for the August bolt shipment. We have reviewed the charges against our purchase order PO-9920 and confirmed that the totals are accurate.

A wire transfer for $18,450 will be [[207]] to your designated account on September 18. [[208]], please note that future invoices should reference both the purchase-order number and the delivery receipt to speed processing.

We appreciate your continued [[209]] as a preferred supplier. [[210]]

questions.explanation: After "will be," the passive past participle "sent" is required: "will be sent to your designated account."
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the base verb "send" or the gerund "sending" where a passive past participle is needed.

questions.explanation: After confirming payment, the letter adds a request that softens into a mild contrast/shift. "However" introduces that procedural note.
questions.commonMistake: Using "Therefore" (result) when the second sentence is a contrasting request, not a consequence of the wire transfer.

questions.explanation: The buyer values the supplier's consistent performance; "reliability" fits a preferred-supplier compliment.
questions.commonMistake: Selecting a similar-looking noun (reliance / reluctance / relevance) that does not praise consistent supplier performance.
